background.text: Jurkat cells were used as a model for lymphocyte activation. Cells were stimulated with anti-CD3/CD28 crosslinking antibodies for 48h to induce a proliferative and activation phenotype, assessed by Ki67 and early apoptosis markers.

objectives: Quantify proliferation in anti-CD3/CD28 stimulated Jurkat cells
Assess early apoptosis by Annexin V co-staining

cells.stimulation: Plate-bound anti-CD3 (1 µg/mL) + soluble anti-CD28 (2 µg/mL), 48h

method.description: After 48h stimulation, cells were harvested and stained for surface markers at 4°C for 30 min. Fixed and permeabilised for intracellular Ki67 staining. Annexin V added in binding buffer. 30,000 events acquired per sample.

results.notes: Ki67+ cells increased from 8% (unstimulated) to 67% (stimulated). CD38 upregulation confirmed. Early apoptosis 11% in stimulated condition.
keyFindings: 67% Ki67+ in stimulated vs 8% in control
Annexin V early apoptosis 11% stimulated vs 4% control

conclusion.summary: Anti-CD3/CD28 stimulation successfully induces proliferation and activation markers in Jurkat cells. Assay suitable for inhibitor screening.
keyFindings: Ki67 and CD38 confirmed as activation readouts
